subject: PHI Control Matrix + BAA redline — Medcord follow-up
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita.rao@medcord.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medcord.com, Mike Levine <mike.levine@medcord.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: PHI handling details + BAA timeline

Jordan — thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Medcord’s security and procurement teams asked me to capture a few follow-ups so we can close the RFP checklist this week:

1) PHI control matrix: can you provide a CSV-level mapping showing where PHI is processed, stored, and logged (inference request, model cache, telemetry, backups)? We need fields, retention, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, and KMS details.

2) BAA: we received your template but Legal has several redlines around subprocessor flow-downs, breach notification timing, and deletion obligations. Can you share your preferred redline versus a clean BAA?

3) Evidence: SOC 2 report (latest), encryption controls summary, and a short dataflow diagram for PHI in hosted vs. private deployments.

Can you confirm an ETA for the items above? Also please include the name and contact for the Redwood person who will sign the BAA (or the delegated authority).

Thanks — we’re aiming to close contract review by next Friday.

—Anita Rao
Director, Security & Compliance
Medcord Health Systems
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Rao <anita.rao@medcord.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PHI handling details + BAA timeline

Anita — thanks for the clear list. Attached are the files you asked for: phi_control_matrix.csv (CSV-level mapping), redwood_baa_initial_redline.docx (our starting redline), and a zip with the RFP artifacts. High-level answers inline below and next steps suggested.

Quick answers:
- PHI processing: inference requests that include PHI are processed in memory; we do not persist model inputs by default in hosted mode. Persistent KV caches are only used for pinned sessions and are encrypted with customer-managed KMS when requested. See phi_control_matrix.csv for per-field handling.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256-GCM at rest. KMS integrations: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS supported.
- Telemetry & logs: request-level telemetry is captured for latency/error monitoring. By default, request bodies are redacted; customers can opt-in to full logging for debugging. Retention defaults to 30 days for telemetry, configurable down to 0 days for Private.
- Subprocessors: list included in the zip. We will flow down PHI obligations to downstream subprocessors in Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers can request a subprocessor addendum.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: send these artifacts (done).
- Wed–Thu: Legal (Marissa) will review Medcord redlines and produce a counter-redline.
- Fri: proposed call to resolve open BAA items and sign-off path.

If you prefer, we can also do a 30-minute call Thursday to walk the control matrix. Available 10–11am PT and 2–4pm PT.

Attachments: phi_control_matrix.csv (CSV), redwood_baa_initial_redline.docx (DOCX), Medcord_RFP_Attachments.zip (ZIP — contains subprocessors list, SOC 2 cover, and architecture diagram)

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Follow-up: PHI handling details + BAA timeline

Anita / Jordan — looping in Legal to summarize our redline rationale so your counsel can triage quickly. Highlights from redwood_baa_initial_redline.docx (summary):

- Breach notification: we propose 72 hours for initial notification for confirmed breaches affecting PHI; 24 hours for active incidents that materially affect service availability. We can negotiate timing language for unknown-scope events.
- Deletion & return of PHI: we include a Customer-Controlled Deletion appendix that clarifies retention windows and API calls to purge cached content.
- Subprocessors: we accept a 30-day notice period for new subprocessors with opt-out rights for enterprise accounts; we will provide the current subprocessors list and commit to flow-down obligations for Dedicated/Private.

Open items we expect Medcord to confirm:
- Desired telemetry retention for hosted (default 30 days vs. 0 days)
- Whether Medcord requires customer-managed KMS in hosted or will accept platform-managed KMS for the pilot

Action: I’ll produce a counter-redline by end of day Thursday and note the clauses we need to escalate (deletion SLA, notification windows). If Medcord legal can flag their top 3 must-haves before then, it will help speed resolution.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PHI control matrix + BAA redline — question on logs

Marissa / Jordan — thanks for the materials. A couple of clarifying questions from Medcord Legal & Security after a first pass:

1) Telemetry/logging: your CSV indicates that request bodies are redacted by default. Can you confirm the mechanism (hashing vs. removal) and whether any identifiers (request_id, user_id) are retained in plaintext within logs? We need the ability to correlate user activity during incident investigations; would a hashed user_id that is reversible only with a KMS key satisfy your needs?

2) Backups & snapshots: do you create persistent snapshots that could contain PHI (e.g., model cache snapshots)? If so, what is the retention and encryption posture for those snapshots?

3) Evidence: please confirm where to download the latest SOC 2 Type II report and whether you can provide an unredacted cover letter for auditor review (we will treat under NDA).

We’d also like to schedule a short legal-to-legal call tomorrow (Thu) to go over redlines and agree on the signatory authority. Please send a DocuSign-ready BAA after counter-redlines so our counsel can accelerate review.

Thanks — I can take a 9–10am PT slot or 3–4pm PT tomorrow.

—Mike Levine
Lead Counsel, Medcord Health Systems
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PHI control matrix + BAA redline — question on logs

Mike / Anita — thanks, and good questions. Short answers below; Marissa and Neha will follow-up with the counter-redline and a DocuSign-ready BAA.

1) Telemetry/logging: default behavior is removal of request bodies; request_id and non-PII metadata (latency, status codes) are retained in plaintext. We support a hashed user_id (SHA-256) option that is reversible only if you provide a customer-managed KMS key (we will not store the plaintext mapping). I’ve attached a short note in the Drive link explaining the reversible-hash pattern we use.

2) Backups/snapshots: we do not snapshot live inference inputs in hosted mode by default. Operator-level snapshots (for infrastructure recovery) can include encrypted volumes; retention is 14 days by default for infra snapshots and they are AES-256-GCM encrypted with platform KMS. For Dedicated/Private, we support customer-managed KMS and configurable retention; we’ll document options in the control matrix.

3) SOC 2: latest report (unredacted cover letter) is available in the Drive folder linked below. For NDA'ed auditor review we can set up temporary access and a secure download.

Next steps / meeting:
- Marissa: counter-redline to Medcord by EOD tomorrow.
- Jordan: will drop DocuSign-ready BAA link into Drive after Marissa’s redline is accounted for.
- Proposed meeting: Fri 10:00am PT — Jordan to send calendar invite if that works.
